**Bornholm: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge** (Bornholm: Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic, Children and Adolescents) is a child and adolescent psychiatric department operating within the Capital Region of Denmark (Region Hovedstaden). The clinic is documented in national quality reports for its stark contrasts in diagnostic and treatment practices for children with ADHD, highlighting significant systemic challenges and resource disparities in regional psychiatric care.

In the context of early diagnostic practices, the clinic reported a 0% fulfillment rate for quality indicator 2a during the 2023/24 reporting period. Specifically, out of 7 eligible cases, none of the children aged 0–5 years received a clinical environmental observation within the required 120 days after the start of the assessment [^src1]. This complete lack of compliance stands in sharp contrast to the national standard of ≥ 90% and underscores severe implementation gaps for early childhood diagnostics on the island of Bornholm [^src1]. The clinic's performance data is systematically reported to the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]], which tracks these regional variations to evaluate diagnostic practices across Danish child psychiatry [^src2].

Conversely, when evaluating treatment metrics, the Bornholm clinic demonstrates a heavy reliance on pharmacological interventions. According to the 2024 national report, the outpatient clinic (listed as B37) recorded the highest medication rate among the mentioned outpatient clinics, with 86% of patients receiving pharmacological treatment [^src2]. This high fulfillment rate for [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] points to a pronounced imbalance in the local ADHD intervention strategy, suggesting that non-pharmacological components may be underutilized or under-resourced compared to medical treatments [^src2]. Together, these metrics paint a picture of a department struggling with early, non-invasive diagnostic observations while heavily defaulting to medical treatment for older cohorts.
